title: Only their empty houses were left standing.
subtitle: The end of Aad, by their Lord's command
then: The wind destroyed everything it was permitted to destroy. Ibn Kathir says {trap}all of them were destroyed, and none were spared.{/trap} Only their homes remained. {idea}This is Allah's way with those who reject His Messengers and disobey Him.{/idea}
now: You drive past a grand old building, now empty, windows boarded. Someone once thought it would hold their name forever. {idea}Walls outlast people, but they do not carry anyone.{/idea} What you build inside yourself is what goes with you.
old: What I build in this world will keep me safe.
new: Buildings can outlast their owners, so my real safety is in how I live before Allah.
try: Next time you pass an old building, think of who built it and what they took with them.

title: They had eyes, ears and hearts, and used none of them.
subtitle: Strength and senses did not save them
then: Ibn Kathir says earlier nations had wealth and children far beyond what the Makkans had. They also had hearing, sight and hearts. {trap}None of it helped, because they used them to deny Allah's signs.{/trap} {idea}The listeners are told to beware of becoming like them.{/idea}
now: You are clever. You can out-argue anyone at dinner. You have a degree, a good salary, a sharp eye. {trap}All of that can be used to avoid the one question that matters.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks what your senses are actually for.{/idea}
old: Being smart and capable keeps me from being misled.
new: Intelligence only helps if I use it to see the truth, not to dodge it.
try: Use your eyes for one sign today: look closely at something living and thank Allah for it.

title: The ruins around you are a message told many ways.
subtitle: Destroyed towns the Makkans passed on trade routes
then: Ibn Kathir lists the towns near Makkah: {trap}Aad, Thamud, Saba, Madyan, and the people of Lut{/trap}, whose places the Makkans passed on their journeys. Allah explained the signs in different ways. {idea}The goal was that perhaps they would return.{/idea}
now: A cousin's divorce. A friend's health scare. A coworker who burned out. You hear these stories every month. {idea}Each one is a quiet sign, explained a different way, so you might turn back sooner.{/idea}
old: Other people's hard lessons are just their stories.
new: The lessons around me are signs repeated in many forms so that I might turn back.
try: Think of one hard thing that happened to someone you know. Write down what it teaches you.

title: Their go-betweens vanished when needed most.
subtitle: What they used to approach Allah left them
then: They claimed these gods were a means of getting closer to Allah. {trap}When the punishment came, the gods did not help; they were simply gone.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says it was their lie, and {trap}they failed in their reliance on them.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself you will get close to Allah once a certain person, a certain mood, a certain trip makes it easier. {idea}You do not need a go-between.{/idea} You can pray right now, from where you are sitting.
old: I need something or someone in between before I can reach Allah.
new: Nothing I invent can bring me near; Allah is reached directly.
try: Make one dua today with no plan and no middle step, just you and Allah.

title: Strangers stopped, hushed each other, and listened.
subtitle: The jinn at Nakhlah hearing the Quran
then: The surah introduction places this on the return from Ta'if, a hard time. Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in prayer at Nakhlah. {idea}A group of jinn stopped, told each other to listen quietly, and heard it through.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said he did not see them. {reward}They went back to warn their own people.{/reward}
now: A recitation plays from a car, a shop, a phone near you. Most people keep talking. {idea}Someone who truly hears says hush, listen.{/idea} Then they carry what they heard home, to a sibling, a child, a friend.
old: When the Quran is playing, I can half-listen while I do other things.
new: The Quran deserves my silence, and what I hear in it is meant to be carried home.
try: Next time you hear the Quran today, stop what you are doing and listen until it ends.

title: We heard a Book after Musa that guides to truth.
subtitle: How the jinn summed up what they heard

row.title: guides
sub: to truth and a straight path

then: Back home, the jinn told their people they had heard a Book sent after Musa. Ibn Kathir notes they named Musa because the Tawrah was the main law before. {idea}It guides to truth in belief and to a straight path in deeds.{/idea} Its information is true and its commands are just.
now: A friend asks what the Quran is really about. You fumble. {idea}The jinn did it in one breath: it confirms what came before, it tells the truth, and it shows the way.{/idea} You can say that too, plainly.
old: I could never explain my faith simply to someone.
new: I can describe the Quran in a few honest words: true in what it says, just in what it asks.
try: Write a two-sentence answer to the question what is the Quran about, in your own words.

title: Answer the caller, and be forgiven and protected.
subtitle: The jinn invite their people
then: The jinn who had just listened now spoke as warners to their own. {idea}Respond to Allah's caller and believe in him.{/idea} {reward}Allah will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.{/reward}
now: You want your brother to come back to prayer. You could list what he does wrong. {reward}Or you could start with how much Allah wants to forgive.{/reward} The jinn, new to faith themselves, led with that.
old: To bring someone back, I need to show them how wrong they are.
new: An invitation can start with forgiveness and safety, not with blame.
try: Share one verse about Allah's forgiveness with someone who might need it today.

title: Ignoring the call does not get you away from Allah.
subtitle: No escape and no protector besides Him
then: The jinn finished their warning plainly. {trap}Whoever does not answer cannot escape on earth and has no protector besides Allah.{/trap} {idea}Such people are in clear error.{/idea}
now: You mute the reminder, change the subject, move to a new city, get very busy. {trap}None of that changes who you answer to.{/trap} {idea}Since you cannot run from Him, the safest place is turning to Him.{/idea}
old: If I stay busy and do not think about it, I am fine.
new: No distance or distraction takes me out of Allah's reach, so I can turn to Him now.
try: Find one reminder you have been snoozing and answer it today, even in a small way.

title: Making the skies did not tire Him; raising the dead will not.
subtitle: Creation as proof of resurrection

row.title: the sky was bigger
sub: He said be, and it was

then: This is said to those who doubted bodies would be raised. Ibn Kathir explains Allah commanded the heavens and earth be, {idea}and they were, with no refusal and no delay. Creating them did not tire Him.{/idea} So bringing the dead back is within His power.
now: You stand at a grave and the mind says: this is the end, how could it be otherwise. {idea}Look up. The sky above that grave was made without effort.{/idea} {reward}Bringing that person back is not harder.{/reward}
old: Bringing the dead back to life seems impossible.
new: If Allah made the heavens without tiring, raising the dead is well within His power.
try: Look at the night sky tonight and remind yourself that its Maker will raise every soul.

title: Is this not the truth? Yes, by our Lord.
subtitle: The confession that comes too late
then: On the Day the deniers face the Fire, they are asked if this is not the truth. Ibn Kathir says the question is: {trap}is this magic, or do you not see?{/trap} {idea}They have no choice but to confess.{/idea} The same word yes, said earlier, would have saved them.
now: You know deep down that something in your life needs to change. One day you will say yes, I knew it. {reward}The gift is saying that yes now, while it can still change things.{/reward}
old: I will admit it when I have to.
new: The yes everyone says in the end is worth far more if I say it now.
try: Admit one truth to yourself today that you already know but keep avoiding.

title: Be patient like the strongest Messengers; life is an hour.
subtitle: Closing comfort for the Prophet ﷺ
then: The surah came in the year of sorrow. Ibn Kathir names those of determination: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. He is told to be patient as they were, and not to hurry the punishment. {idea}On that Day, life will feel like an hour of a day.{/idea}
now: The hard season feels endless: the sick parent, the job search, the long exam year. {idea}Looking back from the Day, all of it will feel like one afternoon.{/idea} {reward}You are in good company in waiting.{/reward}
old: This hard stretch will never end.
new: From the end, this will feel like an hour, and the best of people were patient through theirs.
try: Name your current hard thing, then say: this is one hour, and I will be patient in it.
